coords: three.js: y up, building front faces +z

groundHeights.note: walking surfaces differ by at most 0.1 m; treat as flat y = 0. Every water surface (Water_*) is at y = 0.30 (one reflection plane)

platforms.name: arrival-terrace
platforms.note: outer forecourt, approach and belts at the gate pack's rim level (gate-local 0.869); the gate heightfield (placed at y=-1.517) carries the walker through the passages onto the inner grounds at y=0

topYNote: topY on LOW objects only: block below it, the avatar may land and stand on top; entries without topY block at any height; boxes named water-* are pool/basin interiors (topY = water level)
lawnPolygonOrder: counter-clockwise in the (x, z) plane: shoelace sum(x_i*z_(i+1) - x_(i+1)*z_i) > 0; holes clockwise

spawn.faceYawNote: rotation.y for a character modelled facing +z; pi = facing the building (-z)
spawn.note: on the raised stone approach in front of the gate (it ends near z 352), 40 m south of the door leaves; viewBackM / viewRiseM place the camera behind and above the look-at point at spawn (low rise = nearly level, so the whole gate with its roof is in frame)

sun.convention: three.js world after applying skyRotationDeg. azimuthDeg: 0 = toward +Z, increasing clockwise seen from above (90 = toward -X). direction = unit vector toward the sun = (-sin(az)cos(el), sin(el), cos(az)cos(el)).

skyRotationNote: Apply as scene.backgroundRotation.y = scene.environmentRotation.y = skyRotationDeg * PI/180 (three.js r162+; positive = counter-clockwise seen from above). Derived with three.js equirectUv u = atan2(dir.z, dir.x)/(2PI) + 0.5 from the HDRI's brightest pixel (hdriPixel).
volumesNote: solid boxes for a flying avatar; the colonnade zone and the gate passages stay open

heightfields.note: door leaves ignored: all three passages walkable end to end. USE THIS GRID together with the dynamic 'doors' blockers (closed doors block the passage through the blocker box, open doors let the walker through)
heightfields.format: uint16 little-endian, row-major (row index = z, col index = x)
heightfields.cellCentre: x = originX + (col + 0.5) * cellM ; z = originZ + (row + 0.5) * cellM
heightfields.filledNote: cells inside the rectangle that contain no geometry at all (behind the gate and walls, front corners beyond the curved road) are filled with the height of the nearest low floor (<= 2 m) so that walking in from outside is not blocked

centreLine.note: runs through the full depth of the gate's stone base (z -8.17..+8.17); doorway plane at z 3.35..3.98
